correctness.rationale: The qutrit projective harmonic addition kernel has dimension (q+1)^3 and only three possible overlap values on the four mutually unbiased bases. Three explicit pairwise-orthogonal projectors diagonalize the whole Gram matrix. A standard Legendre recurrence gives exact rational spectra for degrees zero to sixteen; from degree seventeen the provable |P_n(-1/3)|<=1 yields all eigenvalues within 31/[2(q+1)] of one. Consequently the sharp normalized endpoints 2/27 (degree five) and 28/15 (degree four) and the exact maximum condition ratio 63/4 (degree five) follow for every degree, with no extrapolation. The embedded standard-library checker reconstructs 108 exact finite-field overlap comparisons, exact projectors, spectra and certificates.

originality.rationale: The established MUB construction and its projective two-design structure, the Jacobi addition theorem, and their algebraic consequences are credited. The examined primary works do not state sharp all-bidegree qutrit twelve-ray interpolation endpoints or the unique fifth-degree condition maximum. Older Jacobi literature remains a stated residual priority risk; failed searches have not been treated as proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: The full 1975 Delsarte–Goethals–Seidel text was not accessible: an implicit stronger association-scheme corollary remains possible.
Search indices and inspected primary papers cannot establish worldwide publication priority, and unusual naming of projective harmonic evaluation operators may hide an equivalent.
Prior exact two-design analysis establishes low-degree consequences and general Jacobi tools; only the claimed sharp global degree-by-degree constants are advanced as distinct.

value.rationale: A complete qutrit MUB system is a canonical, naturally motivated projective sampling geometry; extending its strength-two tightness to high harmonic bidegrees is a distinct interpolation and stability problem. A full infinite-degree rank classification and the two exact optimal normalized frame bounds reveal a sharp fifth-degree near-degeneracy and a different fourth-degree maximal eigenvalue. This supplies usable minimum-norm interpolation costs and sharp degree selection data, not an arbitrary finite slice or a normalization check.
